title: Puranmashi, the full moon
hookLine: full-moon gatherings recall Guru Nanak's birth at the Katak full moon

lines: ONCE A MONTH, PEOPLE LOOK UP.
BAD PHONE PHOTOS OF THE MOON.
cards: Once a month it happens on the way to the car or out with the trash: the full moon, huge and low and orange over the rooftops. People stop. They take bad phone photos of it.
They text someone: did you see the moon? Strangers on the same sidewalk point it out to each other. For a minute, the sky is the news.
In Sikh communities, that night has a name, and in many places, a gathering. Today: Puranmashi.

teach.b: Puranmashi means the full-moon day. Many gurdwaras hold a special diwan on the full moon each month, with kirtan, katha and langar, sometimes running late into the evening. Why the full moon?
The reason Sikhs give is Guru Nanak.
His birth, his gurpurab, is celebrated on the full moon of the month of Katak, in October or November.

That night, gurdwaras are lit up, processions fill the streets in the days before, and an unbroken reading of the Guru Granth Sahib often ends that morning. So each month's full moon carries a small echo of that one.
Historians add a detail worth knowing: some early accounts of Guru Nanak's life give his birth in the spring month of Vaisakh, not Katak. The Katak full moon is the long-standing tradition.
The sources disagree, and Sikhs have kept the Katak celebration.

teach.h: THE MOON AS A LAMP IN THE AARTI.
teach.b: The moon shines inside the Granth, too. In Guru Nanak's Aarti, on Ang six sixty-three, the whole sky is pictured as a platter for worship.
In paraphrase: the sky is the plate, the sun and moon the lamps, the stars the pearls.
In that picture, the full moon isn't a symbol you have to explain. It's simply one of the lamps the universe holds up to its Creator, and you get to see it.

how: Many gurdwaras hold a monthly Puranmashi diwan on the full moon, with kirtan, katha and langar; Guru Nanak's gurpurab is celebrated on the full moon of Katak.

games.q: it's the Katak full moon. what are Sikhs celebrating?
o: the start of the solar year.
games.why: Guru Nanak's birth is celebrated on the Katak full moon, with lights, processions and readings.

practice: If you can see the moon, go to a window or step outside and look; if it's day or cloudy, picture the last full moon you remember, a lamp held up in a huge silent room.
Breathe slowly while you look, and think of how many people across the world are under the same moon tonight. If you pray, you can say Waheguru, as one more voice in that room.

wordCard.voice: Puranmashi. The full moon, when many gurdwaras gather, echoing Guru Nanak's gurpurab on the full moon of Katak.

carryVoice: Your line: full moon, full heart. The sky has its own aarti. Day six hundred eighty-two, done.
